questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have sought to gain as broad of a series of perspectives as I can throughout my academic life. As this chapter draws to a close, I wanted to come to Japan to experience life here and to explore the different ways they view and encounter academia, life, and politics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a very difficult time with getting the transfers done, and extremely long wait times to hear immediately important information from a few departments on KU's end(although there are some very helpful people who went above and beyond to make sure everything worked out, I am truly grateful for this). This experience made my first month here very, very stressful, especially when combined with Ritsumeikan's rigid class sign-up process. Having a lottery system with no guarantee of even getting access to master's level courses meant I could have been in a situation where I was already in the country and unable to receive credit, as the master's courses are all quite difficult to get a place in. However, this would not be an issue for a bachelor's student. Kyoto is lovely and an amazing place to stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They gave us an informational meeting lasting hours and providing a small book with the necessary information. Although it was far too much for one day, it was comprehensive and the guidebook was helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yes, an orientation seminar.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Like I said, thorough, but overwhelming and very inefficient. I had to go to several appointments, meetings, health exams, and get insurance through the school from multiple places for different types of insurance. It would be far more helpful to just have the insurance in one place, or organized for us to sign up for at orientation.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: very

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's very affordable, but be warned that the showers in the Tokiwa dorm are open, and the general state of the dorm was quite poor. There are great people and very friendly staff though, so I would do it again(if at a different dorm).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: See above with registration issues regarding lottery, etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In most Bachelor's classes, you can just apply. However, most Master's level courses are done via lottery with no guarantee of acceptance, even given the circumstance of needing credits(I talked to the administration here and they would not budge),

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Just the information that we had to do it

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is no advice, but I think the system is worth keeping in mind for the credit transfer process at the master's level.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level was relatively fair, but the overabundance of take-home work meant that most of my time was spent on school rather than exploring around and engaging with Japan. Be prepared to do a lot of writing and presentations.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more homework, seminar, and presentation-focused. There are some very good teachers, and all are quite kind.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global Peace Studies, Local and Regional Development, Migration Studies, Public Diplomacy, Intensive Japanese I(Non-credit, Bachelors level class taken to fill hour requirements at host institution)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Public Diplomacy is great and I learned a ton, but it is a lot of work. Migration Studies and Global Peace studies were great

questions.answer: The insurance and registration fees were not anticipated

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruit is far more expensive than I would have thought. Otherwise most other things are cheaper due to the great exchange rate. Bullet Trains are also very expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They did not advertise clubs at all(this is apparently done in the spring, and I did not know we had many), just the study abroad program events.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Events are normally planned by dorms or the study abroad faculty.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: hiking, exploring, and trying new foods! Take weekend trips to get a break from school.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Weekend trips, and take days to relax.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, but there are lots of little cultural shifts that can add up and be difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the izakayas and just be open to new experiences! Talk to the people around you, especially during orientation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Walking on the left side of the path and the overemphasis on seeming productive were the most difficult. There is also a lot of Xenophobia in Kyoto due to the overabundance of tourists, and I had several bad experiences with antagonistic people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The strive for quality in everything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The most important, and I believe the only key thing, is to just go. Youll be a better and more rounded person with a new treasure of stories and friends that you will have for the rest of your life. Second, eat as many local dishes as you can. Last, make time for yourself too so you can destress and not get overwhelmed.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: n/a

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends whom I will miss dearly.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The overwhelming, yet not difficult amount of school work given. Again, nothing was hard, everything just took a very long time to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: n/a

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
